rationale: The article tests small marginal signal from Driver category support after race/tyre-state features under a fixed OOF counterfactual. The existing body cover is a crowded character/telemetry montage with unrelated numeric displays, so a clean technical overview is clearer and avoids implying unsupported measured performance. A neutral race car and race-state plus category-count cards feed a five-fold comparison. The targeted edit replaced assistance-team icons with category-frequency rows and removed the weather symbol; all existing body imagery remains unchanged.
alt_en: Race-state and driver-category support features enter a controlled out-of-fold tree-model comparison.
alt_ko: 주행 상태와 드라이버 범주의 표본 수 피처를 같은 OOF 조건에서 비교하는 트리 모델 구성.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: wide landscape cover for a technical machine-learning article, approximately 1.9:1 aspect ratio.
Primary request: a clear professional scientific illustration of driver-feature engineering for Formula 1 pit-stop prediction, emphasizing controlled out-of-fold comparison instead of driver skill or glamorous racing.
Scene/backdrop: clean white or pale off-white background, no circuit scenery.
Subject and topology: at the left, one modest technically recognizable top-down open-wheel racing car, drawn as a precise slate-blue silhouette with four distinct tyres and no livery. Beside the car, two compact feature cards: one headed "Race state" showing three unlabeled rows with small tyre/lap pictograms; one headed "Driver support" showing a simple category-count glyph, not a portrait. Thin arrows from both cards converge into one clean five-segment held-out validation strip at center-right, four pale slate segments and one teal segment. Below that strip, one pair of visually identical small branching-tree models side by side evokes a controlled counterfactual comparison; do not show either model winning. Above the strip use the single label "OOF validation".
Style/medium: refined technical editorial illustration with crisp flat shapes, precise scientific linework, sparse annotations; a cover concept, not an empirical dashboard.
Composition/framing: wide horizontal canvas around 1.9:1, car and features on the first half, validation on the second half, clear hierarchy, ample white space, visually coherent rather than a collage. Large labels and recognisable car/tyres remain readable when reduced.
Palette: white/off-white, deep slate #32465A, muted blue #7298B5, restrained teal #458D8B. Professional and low saturation.
Text: only the exact three large labels "Race state", "Driver support", and "OOF validation". No other text or numbers.
Constraints: no invented lap times, driver names, IDs, scores, percentages, measured curves, performance ranking, victory claim, championship trophy, copied F1 or Kaggle logo, logos, watermark, dense dashboards, tiny labels, people, ducks, mascots, glamorous rendering, glossy 3D or abstract essay metaphors. Deliver one finished cover illustration, not a page mockup.
editing_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the edit target. Keep the wide composition, racing car, all arrows, five-part validation strip, both tree models, palette, white background, and the exact three existing text labels unchanged.
Change only the pictograms inside the two feature cards so they correctly represent statistical features. In the card titled "Driver support", remove the gear, wrench and laptop and their connecting branches; replace all of them with a simple category-frequency table glyph: three clean horizontal rows, each with one small empty square category token and a short muted-blue horizontal support-count bar, no letters or numbers. Here "support" means the number of dataset rows per driver category, never mechanics assisting a driver.
In the card titled "Race state", keep the tyre pictogram and the checkered lap/progress pictogram; replace the rain-cloud pictogram in the bottom row with a simple pair of stacked tyres representing a stint/tyre-state variable. Do not add weather variables.
This remains a conceptual scientific illustration, not an empirical chart; do not add values, performance results, new labels, icons outside the cards, watermarks or logos. Everything outside these two card pictograms must be preserved.
